import pandas as pd

def run(inputs: dict) -> dict:
    target_snapshot = inputs["target_snapshot"].copy()
    cdc_events = inputs["cdc_events"].copy()
    watermark = inputs["watermark"].copy()

    # Determine watermark timestamp
    high_ts = watermark["high_ts"].iloc[0]

    # Step 1: keep only events strictly after the watermark
    filtered = cdc_events[cdc_events["event_ts"] > high_ts].copy()

    if not filtered.empty:
        # Step 2: latest event per product_id by (event_ts, event_seq)
        filtered = filtered.sort_values(["event_ts", "event_seq"])
        latest = filtered.groupby("product_id", as_index=False).last()
    else:
        latest = filtered  # empty frame with same columns

    # Build a working dict keyed by product_id from the target snapshot
    target_indexed = target_snapshot.set_index("product_id", drop=False)

    for _, row in latest.iterrows():
        pid = row["product_id"]
        op = row["op"]
        if op == "D":
            if pid in target_indexed.index:
                target_indexed = target_indexed.drop(index=pid)
        else:
            new_row = {
                "product_id": pid,
                "name": row["name"],
                "price": row["price"],
                "last_event_ts": row["event_ts"],
            }
            target_indexed.loc[pid] = new_row

    new_snapshot = target_indexed.reset_index(drop=True)

    # Ensure column order matches target_snapshot schema
    new_snapshot = new_snapshot[["product_id", "name", "price", "last_event_ts"]]

    # Preserve dtypes as close as possible to original schema
    new_snapshot["product_id"] = new_snapshot["product_id"].astype("int64")
    new_snapshot["price"] = new_snapshot["price"].astype("float64")
    new_snapshot["last_event_ts"] = pd.to_datetime(new_snapshot["last_event_ts"]).astype("datetime64[us]")

    return {"new_snapshot": new_snapshot}
